messages.subject: Re: Layered Bar Charts
parts:
Hmmm, I don't see any easy way of doing this because the final nested
bar needs to be both stacked and dodged. Two options:

* switch to using facetting instead of dodging
* try the productplots package - http://vita.had.co.nz/papers/prodplots.html

Hadley

On Tue, Mar 27, 2012 at 8:55 PM, Kim <kim.fe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dear ggplot2 group,
>
> I am trying to create the following plot.
> 1. A dodged bar chart with Factor 'Level1' (containing the levels
> 'L11', 'L12', and 'L13') on the x axis and N on the Y axis
> 2. Within each bar for L11, L12, and L13, I would like to have dodged
> bar charts of Factor 'Level 2' (containing the levels 'L2F1', 'L2F2',
> and 'L2F3')
> 3. Within L2F1, I'd like to have a stacked bar chart of L2F1's levels
> (Low, Medium, High).  Within L2F2 and L2F3, I'd like to have a stacked
> bar chart of their levels (0, and 1).
>
> Here is my code so far. p2 looks just like I'd like it to
> (corresponding to Step 2 above), but it is p3 that does not work
> (corresponding to step 3 above) - I'm not sure how to code it.  Can
> anyone help me with the code to plot  stacked factor levels
> corresponding to the L2F1, L2F2, and L2F3 variables within L11, L12,
> and L13?
>
> Any help is greatly appreciated.  Thanks so much!
>
> Kim
> ------------------------
> #Make a dataset for each hierarchical level
> df1 <- read.csv(textConnection("
>  Level1,N
>  L11,120
>  L12,120
>  L13,120"))
>
> df2 <- read.csv(textConnection("
>  Level1,Level2,N
>  L11,L2F1,60
>  L12,L2F1,60
>  L13,L2F1,60
>  L11,L2F2,30
>  L12,L2F2,30
>  L13,L2F2,30
>  L11,L2F3,30
>  L12,L2F3,30
>  L13,L2F3,30"))
>
> df3 <- read.csv(textConnection("
>  Level1, Level2,FactorVal, N
>  L11,L2F1,Low,10
>  L11,L2F1,Med,20
>  L11,L2F1,High,30
>  L12,L2F1,Low,10
>  L12,L2F1,Med,20
>  L12,L2F1,High,30
>  L13,L2F1,Low,10
>  L13,L2F1,Med,20
>  L13,L2F1,High,30
>  L11,L2F2,0,10
>  L11,L2F2,1,20
>  L12,L2F2,0,10
>  L12,L2F2,1,20
>  L13,L2F2,0,10
>  L13,L2F2,1,20
>  L11,L2F3,0,10
>  L11,L2F3,1,20
>  L12,L2F3,0,10
>  L12,L2F3,1,20
>  L13,L2F3,0,10
>  L13,L2F3,1,20"))
>
> closeAllConnections()
>
> p <- ggplot(df1)
> p1 <- p  + geom_bar(data = df1, aes(Level1, N), stat = "identity")
> p2 <- p1 + geom_bar(data = df2, aes(Level1, N, fill = Level2),
> stat="identity",position="dodge")
> p3 <- p2 + geom_bar(data = df3, aes(Level1, N, fill =
> FactorVal,weight=Level2,group=Level2,position="stack"), stat =
> "identity")
> p3
>
